units.text: INT. ROOFTOP GREENHOUSE - SUNSET
A glass shed on the roof of a tenement, filled with tomato plants, geraniums, and a sagging lawn chair.
The city sprawls beyond the panes, rose-gold in the last light.
A tape recorder sits on an upturned crate with its lid open.
The door creaks.
ADAEZE NWOSU, 30s, in a long cardigan and paint-spattered jeans, steps inside carrying a watering can.
She is tired in the way of someone who has decided to be tired quietly.
She sets the can down.
Looks at the recorder.
Kneels beside it.
She presses a button.
The tape whirs.
Okay. It's me. Again. I know you said not to.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: She laughs without humor and rubs her eyes.
I'm on the roof. The tomatoes are doing better than I am. I thought you'd want to know.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: She waits.
A silence stretches.
A pigeon lands on the glass, scuttles, leaves.
She presses stop.
Rewinds.
Presses play.
Okay. It's me. I'm just going to talk. Don't answer. Don't ever answer. I just need to say these things aloud to somebody who isn't me.
units.name: ADAEZE
paren: from the tape, a month old

units.text: She switches the tape off.
Sits on the lawn chair.
Takes up the recorder in her lap.
Right. Here's what I wanted to say.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: She presses record.
A long breath.

I think I loved you the way people love a house they've never entered. I stood outside admiring the porch. I never tried the door. And when you finally opened it, I was so busy looking at the porch that I didn't walk in.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: She switches the recorder off.
Watches a bee drift between flowers.
She rewinds again.
Presses play, and listens to herself.
That's all. I don't expect anything. I just wanted the tomatoes to know you were here once.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: Adaeze exhales.
She stands, takes up the watering can, and pours water at the base of each plant, slowly, one by one.
The sun slides lower.
The glass turns copper.
When she is done she sets the can down.
Returns to the recorder.
Presses record.
It's me. I'm going to leave a message. I know you won't listen. But I'm going to say it anyway.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: She takes a long breath.
I was wrong about the house. It isn't a house. It's a greenhouse. Everything in it is trying to grow toward the glass. And I stood here for years wondering why it was so bright.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: A beat.
She smiles at herself.
So here is my invitation. No porch. No door. Just the roof. Come up. Come up and see what I've done with the tomatoes.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: She presses stop.
Ejects the cassette.
Holds it in her palm, small and warm in the fading light.
She slips it into an envelope on the crate.
Seals it.
Writes a name on the front, in careful hand, then crosses it out and writes another.
Nothing in her face tells which.
She sets the envelope on the lawn chair, propped against the arm, where the last orange light finds it.
Then she turns off the lamp, and stands for a while in the half dark among the green.
A siren sounds in the street below.
She does not move toward it.
The tomatoes rustle in the breeze from a cracked pane.
Adaeze steps outside.
The door closes behind her, softly, as though not to wake something.
The envelope rests in its pool of dying gold.
